title: Slack website, 2018
lede: Slack’s 2018 home page: four flat, long-limbed people work around an oversized chat window beside the serif headline “Where Work Happens”.
summary: Flat figures with long limbs and natural skin around an oversized chat window; light hatch texture. 2018.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. No cookie box covers the page. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.

styles.note: Borderline: the figures are flat and long-limbed and act around an oversized interface, but their skin is natural and parts carry a hatch texture. Wired names Slack among the brands that use the style.

notice: The live Slack site has changed since this 2018 capture.
context: Alice Lee made the illustration voice and library for Slack from January 2017, citing Mary Blair and Charley Harper, with “organic, imperfect shapework; bold colors and warm tone”. [Alice Lee](https://www.byalicelee.com/slack).
Wired (2021) lists Slack among the brands that use the style. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/corporate-memphis-design-tech/).
observed: On the left, a large chat window titled “#project-mobile” shows colored squares and grey placeholder lines, with a dark plum bar at its left edge.

Four people stand, kneel, and walk around it: a red-haired woman in a blue jacket and a yellow and green skirt, a kneeling woman writing on the window, and a man in a green sweater holding up a chart.
Skin tones are natural browns and peach. Limbs are long and figures are about eight heads tall; faces have small features.
The kneeling woman’s top and the man’s trousers carry a fine grid or hatch texture.
On the right, “Where Work Happens” is set in a heavy serif, with an email field and a square indigo button.
interpretation: It shows the style’s layout and gesture (people acting on a giant interface) without its non-natural skin. The heavy serif headline and square button also depart from the style’s rounded sans-serif interface.
borrow: Put the figures around an oversized version of the product’s own window so the illustration explains the product.

images.alt: Slack home page, 2018: four flat, long-limbed people with natural skin work around a large chat window on the left; the heavy serif headline “Where Work Happens” and an email sign-up on the right.
